turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Why do you refuse to play with me, boy?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Miss Havisham, it's not that I don't want to play, it's just that...

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Speak, boy, speak!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid my sister is ill and I must go to her, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Ill? What a trifling thing is illness compared to the weight of years and the burden of a broken heart.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham, I'm afraid it's very serious.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I am not interested in your sister's health, boy. I am interested in your refusal to play with me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not refusing, Miss Havisham, I'm just...

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Silence, boy! You will not speak to me in that tone.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm sorry, Miss Havisham, I didn't mean to offend you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Call Estella, boy. I will not be ignored.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Miss Havisham, I think it would be better if I went home now.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: No, boy, you will not go. You will stay and play with me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But Miss Havisham, I really must go.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will do as I say, boy. You will play with Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't know if that's such a good idea, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: What do you mean, boy? Estella is a lady and you are a gentleman. You will play with her.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But Miss Havisham, I'm not very good at playing games.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I do not care about your abilities, boy. I only care that you play with Estella.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'll try my best, Miss Havisham.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip who it was.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip told Miss Havisham that he was Mr. Pumblechook's boy and had come to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to come nearer and let her look at him.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was afraid of a woman who had never seen the sun since he was born.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not afraid.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he knew what she touched when she touched her heart.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Pip replied that he knew it was her heart.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham exclaimed that her heart was broken.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip that she was tired and wanted diversion.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham said that she sometimes had sick fancies and had a sick fancy that she wanted to see some play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham repeatedly told Pip to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham asked Pip if he was sullen and obstinate.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Pip replied that he was not sullen and obstinate, but was very sorry for Miss Havisham and could not play just now.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Miss Havisham ordered Pip to call Estella.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Miss Havisham told Pip to call Estella, who was at the door.
